examples.name: H563 LED blink (PA5, CN7 pin 10)
examples.description: SysTick firmware toggles PA5 every 100 ms; 330 Ω and a red LED to ground. LED brightness follows the solved current.

examples.name: H563 RC button to EXTI (PA6, CN9 pin 1)
examples.description: Hold the push button: a 10 kΩ/100 kΩ divider charges 100 nF on PA6; each Schmitt crossing interrupts the firmware, which mirrors PA6 onto the PA5 LED.

examples.name: DC divider
examples.description: Analog only: 5 V across 2 kΩ + 3 kΩ; the midpoint must read 3 V.

examples.name: RC charge through a switch
examples.description: Analog only: hold the button to charge 10 µF through 1 kΩ (τ = 10 ms); release and it holds its charge.

examples.name: NPN low-side LED switch
examples.description: Analog only: the button drives 10 kΩ into a 2N3904-like base; the transistor saturates and sinks the LED current through 220 Ω.

examples.name: H563 I²C/SPI/UART bus demo
examples.description: Firmware talks to a 24C02 EEPROM and a TMP102 on I2C1, reads a W25Q flash JEDEC ID on SPI1 and sends 'ping' to a USB-UART adapter on USART2; results print on USART3. Remove a pull-up or an SDA wire to see BUSY or NACK.

examples.name: U585 I²C/SPI bus demo
examples.description: The H563 bus demo firmware built for the STM32U585: a 24C02 EEPROM and a TMP102 on I2C1, a W25Q flash JEDEC ID on SPI1. Results print on USART3.

examples.name: N657 I²C/SPI bus demo
examples.description: The bus demo on the NUCLEO-N657X0-Q Arduino headers: a 24C02 EEPROM and a TMP102 on I2C1 (D15/D14), a W25Q flash JEDEC ID on SPI5 (D13-D10). Results print on USART1.

examples.name: H563 secure elements (ATECC608A, SE050, STSAFE-A120)
examples.description: The secure element suite asks an ATECC608A on SPI1 for its revision and random bytes, resets an SE050 on I2C1 and runs Echo and GenerateRandom on an STSAFE-A120 on I2C2; m33mu's own device models answer. Results print on USART3. Unplug a module's VCC to see it NACK.

examples.name: Pico 2 GPIO: button on GP15 lights GP16
examples.description: RP2350 firmware blinks the on-board LED (GPIO25) every 50 ms and copies GP15 to GP16: the internal pull-up keeps GP15 high and the green LED on, pressing the button pulls GP15 low and the LED goes off.

examples.name: H563 user button B1 lights LD1
examples.description: No circuit: press and hold the blue B1 button on the board drawing; the firmware copies PC13 to the green LD1 (PB0).

examples.name: nRF5340 DK GPIO: D2 switch lights D3, Button 1 lights LED1
examples.description: Firmware copies Arduino D2 (P1.04, pull-up) to D3 (P1.05): the green LED is on until you press the switch. Hold Push button 1 on the board strip and LED 0 (P0.28, active low) lights.

examples.name: H563 timer PWM (LD1 breathing, D9 RC filter)
examples.description: TIM3_CH3 on PB0 breathes the on-board green LD1; TIM4_CH4 on PD15 (CN7 pin 18, D9) is a 1 kHz, 25 % PWM into 10 kΩ/1 µF, which settles near 0.83 V. Scope CH1 shows the PWM, CH2 the filtered output.

examples.name: Op-amp non-inverting gain ×2
examples.description: Analog only: 1 V input, 5 V single supply and 10 kΩ/10 kΩ feedback produce about 2 V at the loaded output. The macro model has finite rail swing and output resistance.

examples.name: H563 ADC + FFT (signal generator, op-amp level shifter, A0)
examples.description: A ±1 V sine from the function generator is inverted and centred on 1.65 V by an op-amp (gain −1, IN+ biased to 0.825 V by 30 kΩ/10 kΩ from 3V3) and sampled on A0 at 8 kHz. The firmware prints the DC level and the strongest FFT peaks on USART3. Change the waveform or frequency and watch the spectrum follow.
